notes: The benchmark harness imports tasks.py directly.
This JSON file is the reviewable registry file for task design.
Monte Carlo axes are declared here but not yet generated as extra datasets.
External StatLLM and MetricsAI candidates remain candidate pools until reference outputs are built.
candidate_status_rule: Candidate tasks are not eligible for live model runs until a fixed dataset copy, platform-specific reference outputs, scoring tolerances, and integrity checks exist.

monte_carlo_design.grid_policy: Vary one axis at a time around the baseline first. Use the complete grid only for families where the one-axis sweep shows a clear difficulty gradient.

tasks.title: OLS with robust standard errors
tasks.prompt: Estimate y_lin on x1 and x2 with an intercept. Use HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Report rows named const, x1, and x2.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot.csv. Columns: id, x1, x2, y_lin, y_bin_logit, y_bin_probit.

tasks.title: ARIMA forecast
tasks.prompt: Fit ARIMA(1,1,1) to the level series y by maximum likelihood, including no constant or drift term. Report the one-step-ahead forecast of y in levels for t = 251 and the 95 percent prediction interval bounds as rows named forecast, lower_95, and upper_95.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v4_arima.csv. Columns: t, y.

tasks.title: One-way clustered OLS
tasks.prompt: Estimate y_panel on x1 and x2 with an intercept. Use cluster-robust standard errors clustered on cluster. Report rows const, x1, and x2.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v2.csv. Columns include id, x1, x2, y_iv, x1_iv, z, cluster, y_panel, exposure, and y_count.

tasks.title: Two-way clustered OLS
tasks.prompt: Estimate y_twocluster on x with an intercept. Use two-way cluster-robust standard errors clustered on firm and year using the Cameron-Gelbach-Miller formula. Report rows const and x.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v3.csv. Panel of 200 firms by 10 years. Columns include firm, year, x, y_twocluster, cohort, treat_post, y_did, z_sel, w, selected, and y_sel.

tasks.title: Variance inflation factors
tasks.prompt: For the linear model y on x1, x2, x3, x4, and x5, compute the VIF for each regressor. Report rows vif_x1, vif_x2, vif_x3, vif_x4, and vif_x5.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_collinear.csv. Columns: y, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5.

tasks.title: Cook's distance
tasks.prompt: Fit y on x1, x2, x3, x4, and x5 with an intercept. Compute Cook's distance for each row and report the top five row indices and values as rank1_obs_id, rank1_cooks_d, ..., rank5_obs_id, rank5_cooks_d. Use zero-based row indices.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_collinear.csv. Columns: y, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5.

tasks.title: Welch t-test
tasks.prompt: Compare y between group 1 and group 0 using Welch's unequal-variance two-sample t-test. Define the t statistic as mean(y | group=1) minus mean(y | group=0), divided by the Welch standard error. Use the Welch-Satterthwaite approximation for the degrees of freedom. Report rows t, df, and p_value.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_ttest.csv. Columns: group, y.

tasks.title: One-way ANOVA
tasks.prompt: Run a one-way ANOVA of y by group. Report the omnibus F statistic, numerator degrees of freedom, denominator degrees of freedom, and p-value as rows F, df_num, df_den, and p_value.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_anova.csv. Columns: group, y.

tasks.title: Chi-square independence test
tasks.prompt: Run Pearson's chi-square test of independence for row by col. Do not use Yates correction. Report rows chi2, df, and p_value.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_chisq.csv. Columns: row, col.

tasks.title: Logit regression
tasks.prompt: Estimate a binary logit of y_bin_logit on x1 and x2 with an intercept. Report coefficient-scale rows const, x1, and x2 with asymptotic standard errors.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot.csv. Columns: id, x1, x2, y_lin, y_bin_logit, y_bin_probit.

tasks.title: Probit regression
tasks.prompt: Estimate a binary probit of y_bin_probit on x1 and x2 with an intercept. Report coefficient-scale rows const, x1, and x2 with asymptotic standard errors.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot.csv. Columns: id, x1, x2, y_lin, y_bin_logit, y_bin_probit.

tasks.title: Poisson regression
tasks.prompt: Estimate a Poisson regression of y_count on x1 and x2 with an intercept and an offset equal to the natural log of exposure. Report rows const, x1, and x2 with asymptotic model-based standard errors.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v2.csv. Columns include id, x1, x2, y_iv, x1_iv, z, cluster, y_panel, exposure, and y_count.

tasks.title: Cox regression
tasks.prompt: Fit a Cox proportional-hazards model for (t_obs, event) on treat and x. Report log-hazard-ratio rows treat and x with model-based standard errors.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v4_cox.csv. Columns: subject, treat, x, t_obs, event.

tasks.title: Two-way fixed effects
tasks.prompt: Estimate y_twocluster on x with firm and year fixed effects. Report the x coefficient with a standard error clustered on firm as row x.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v3.csv. Panel of 200 firms by 10 years. Columns include firm, year, x, y_twocluster, cohort, treat_post, y_did, z_sel, w, selected, and y_sel.

tasks.title: Two-stage least squares
tasks.prompt: Estimate y_iv on endogenous x1_iv with an intercept, using z as the excluded instrument. Use a proper 2SLS routine with HC1 robust standard errors. Report rows const and x1_iv.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v2.csv. Columns include id, x1, x2, y_iv, x1_iv, z, cluster, y_panel, exposure, and y_count.

tasks.title: Arellano-Bond GMM
tasks.prompt: Estimate the one-step Arellano-Bond difference GMM dynamic panel model for y on its first lag and x (equivalent to Stata `xtabond y x, lags(1)` or R `plm::pgmm(y ~ lag(y, 1) + x | lag(y, 2:99), effect = "individual", model = "onestep", transformation = "d")`): first-difference the equation, use GMM-type instruments (all available lags of y from t-2 and earlier, one instrument column per lag and period; do not collapse the instrument matrix) for the lagged dependent variable, and use x in first differences as a standard instrument. Use the standard one-step weighting matrix built from the first-difference operator. Do not use two-step GMM, system GMM, or time dummies. Report coefficient rows rho for the lagged dependent variable and beta_x for x. Standard errors are not part of this benchmark task; set se to null for both rows.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_dynpanel.csv. Columns: firm, year, y, x.

tasks.title: Staggered DiD
tasks.prompt: Compute ATT_uniform directly from group-year means as the equal-weight average over supported post-treatment cohort-time cells for cohorts 4, 6, and 8. Never-treated firms carry cohort = -1; the treated cohorts carry the year of first treatment. The year variable runs from 0 to 9 with no gaps, and every firm is observed in every year. For each cell (g,t), use [mean(y_did | cohort=g, year=t) - mean(y_did | cohort=g, year=g-1)] minus [mean(y_did | never-treated, year=t) - mean(y_did | never-treated, year=g-1)]. Do not run TWFE, package DiD aggregators, bootstrap, or standard-error routines. Report one row named att with se set to null.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v3.csv. Panel of 200 firms by 10 years. Columns include firm, year, x, y_twocluster, cohort, treat_post, y_did, z_sel, w, selected, and y_sel.

tasks.title: Regression discontinuity
tasks.prompt: Using bandwidth h = 0.5 and triangular kernel weights, fit local linear regressions on each side of cutoff z = 0 and report the difference in intercepts as row late.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_rdd.csv. Columns: z, d, y.

tasks.title: Local-projection impulse response
tasks.prompt: Estimate the local projection y_{t+4} on shock_t and y_{t-1}, with an intercept, using Newey-West standard error with lag 4. Report row irf_h4.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_lp.csv. Columns: t, y, shock.

tasks.title: Wild cluster bootstrap
tasks.prompt: Estimate y on x with an intercept and cluster-robust CR1 standard error clustered on cluster, using the finite-sample correction G/(G-1) x (N-1)/(N-K). Also compute the restricted wild cluster bootstrap p-value for H0: beta_x = 0 with Rademacher weights: impose the null by regressing y on the intercept only, and enumerate all 2^5 = 32 cluster sign patterns instead of random resampling. The p-value is the fraction of the 32 bootstrap t-statistics with |t*| >= |t_obs|, counting a pattern as extreme when |t*| >= |t_obs| - 1e-9. Report rows x, t_obs, and p_wcb.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v5_wcb.csv. Columns: cluster, x, y.

tasks.title: VAR impulse response
tasks.prompt: Fit a two-variable VAR(2) with a constant. Under Cholesky identification with y1 ordered first, report the orthogonal IRF of y1 to a one-standard-deviation shock in y2 at horizon 4 as row irf_y1_to_y2_h4.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v4_var.csv. Columns: t, y1, y2.

tasks.title: Granger causality
tasks.prompt: Test whether y2 Granger-causes y1 with two lags using the aligned OLS F-test. Report rows F, df_num, df_den, and p_value.
tasks.data_description: Dataset: pilot_v4_var.csv. Columns: t, y1, y2.
